sampling_model.design: Randomized binary treatment with known allocation probability \(\pi\in[\pi_0,1-\pi_0]\).
sampling_model.units: Independent draws of \(O=(A,X,Y)\) from the observed Gaussian law \(P_{\vartheta}\) indexed by \(\vartheta\in\Theta\); ordinary Wald inference is restricted to \(\Theta_+(\nu_*)\), while projection inference and the angular frontier retain their stated whole-class domains.
sampling_model.overlap: The allocation probability is uniformly separated from zero and one.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The finite-dimensional map \(\theta(P)\) is estimated from arm-specific means, variances, and outcome-covariances and the pooled covariate covariance on an evaluation split independent of covariate selection.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The underlying conditional-optimal-transport information model requires a shared covariate marginal and motivates variable selection; compact-support assumptions used by particular published theorems do not themselves cover the Gaussian frontier class.
Sparse covariance eigenvalues lower-bound the regression submodularity ratio and yield a forward-selection approximation guarantee.
Submodularity ratio and generalized curvature jointly yield a tight generic cardinality-constrained greedy guarantee.
Multiplier-bootstrap aggregation permits valid covariate and model selection among conditional-transport dual bounds.
A smooth-density quadratic conditional-transport estimator has a fixed-target central limit theorem away from equality.
A short never-empty confidence interval is valid when estimated lower and upper bounds have a regular joint Gaussian limit.

body.tldr: For a randomized Gaussian experiment, the observed-law functional \(B(S)\) is the sharp conditional-optimal-transport lower endpoint for the causal estimand \(\tau_2\), not the estimand itself. Its increment is a squared chordal distance between upper-hemisphere lifts of residualized arm-score vectors. Writing \(K=M/m\) and \(R=V/s\), the exact fixed-budget submodularity-ratio frontier is \(\rho_k(K,R)=1\) when \(k=1\) or \(R=1\), and \(\rho_k(K,R)=k/\{1+(k-1)KR\}\) when \(k\ge2\) and \(R>1\). Hence population forward greedy attains the exact certified factor \(1-\{1-\rho_k(K,R)/k\}^k\), with the corresponding empirical additive-error guarantee. Unequal-scale Gaussian families attain the frontier in the limit, and the optimal dimension-free limit is \(1/(KR)\) for \(R>1\). Generic greedy analysis and sample-split post-selection inference are credited prior machinery; the new contribution is the sharp Gaussian budget frontier. Independent evaluation gives Wald inference on the separated parameter image and a conservative raw-moment projection interval over the whole compact image, including equality laws.

project_justification.gap: Conditional optimal transport supplies sharp covariate-assisted causal bounds, but existing work treats the conditioning set as fixed. Generic weak-submodularity results provide greedy recurrences without determining the exact approximation ratio of the unequal-scale two-arm Gaussian endpoint. In particular, neither the fixed-set Gaussian formulas nor one-response regression theory yields the piecewise fixed-budget frontier \(\rho_k(K,R)\).
project_justification.niche: The Gaussian endpoint has a residual-score geometry that is absent from one-response regression: singleton and joint gains are chordal distances observed through a sparse Schur-complement frame.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the residual angular identity, proves the exact frontier \(\rho_k(K,R)=1\) for \(k=1\) or \(R=1\) and \(\rho_k(K,R)=k/\{1+(k-1)KR\}\) for \(k\ge2\), \(R>1\), and constructs fully randomized unequal-scale Gaussian laws approaching it. Substitution into the standard recurrence gives the exact certified greedy factor \(1-\{1-\rho_k(K,R)/k\}^k\); the optimal budget- and dimension-uniform limit is \(1/(KR)\) when \(R>1\). The project also specializes credited independent-sample Wald inference to the separated image and supplies conservative moment-projection inference on the full compact image.

body.related_work: Lin, Gao, Blanchet, and Glynn (2025) motivate covariate-assisted conditional transport, prove interpolation toward the conditional bound, give Gaussian benchmarks, and identify variable selection as future work. Here \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Lin}}\) denotes their underlying common-pretreatment-marginal information model; it is distinct from the compact-support and regularity class imposed by particular theorems in that paper. The present sparse-margin Gaussian class is a proper subclass of that underlying information model. Accordingly, its approximation lower bound does not transfer to every law in the broader information model, and its adverse Gaussian converse does not transfer to the compact-support theorem class without a separate truncation or approximation argument. Lin et al. (2026) establish sharp fixed-information bounds and adapted-Wasserstein estimation, and their smooth-density work gives rates and a fixed-target quadratic central limit theorem. Das and Kempe (2011) introduce the submodularity ratio and sparse-spectral control for regression; Bian et al. (2017) and Elenberg et al. (2018) provide generic greedy and restricted-curvature machinery. Those works supply credited optimization machinery, whereas the exact two-arm frontier here is model-specific. Ji, Lei, and Spector (2023) supply generic selection-valid inference among covariate and model choices, so sample splitting and post-selection validity are not novelty claims. Gelbrich (1990) and Fang and Zhu (2020) describe covariance-transport geometry beyond Gaussian laws, without automatically preserving the conditional sparse-selection calculation. Imbens and Manski (2004) and Stoye (2021) motivate honest inference at partial-identification boundaries; the whole-image projection interval follows that conservative principle without a claim of length optimality.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The unequal-scale sharpness family has a positive but vanishing endpoint contrast as \(h\downarrow0\). This is sufficient to attain the submodularity-ratio frontier, but it does not exhibit a worst-case greedy-value ratio at fixed signal amplitude. More generally, exact sharpness of \(\rho_k(K,R)\) and the induced certified factor does not prove that the greedy-value factor itself is attained by a law in the class. Ordinary Wald inference is asserted only on the separated image \(\Theta_+(\nu_*)\); equality laws have zero endpoint contrast and degenerate first-order endpoint variance and are handled by conservative whole-image moment projection. Computing or certifying the best sparse margins may itself be combinatorial, so \(m,M,s,V\) are treated as certified inputs. No transfer of the Gaussian converse to the compact-support theorem class of Lin et al. is claimed without a separate approximation argument.
body.honest_scope: The exact fixed-budget frontier is proved over the explicitly quantified randomized Gaussian sparse-margin classes: \(\rho_k(K,R)=1\) for \(k=1\) or \(R=1\), and \(\rho_k(K,R)=k/\{1+(k-1)KR\}\) for \(k\ge2\), \(R>1\). Its exact induced greedy certificate is \(1-\{1-\rho_k(K,R)/k\}^k\), obtained from credited generic weak-submodularity machinery. For \(R>1\), the optimal certificate uniform over dimensions and budgets is the limit \(1/(KR)\). The extremal construction specifies the Gaussian covariate law, independent arm noises, independent \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) assignment, potential outcomes, and observed outcome, but approaches the frontier with vanishing signal and does not establish attainment of the worst-case greedy-value ratio at fixed signal. The Gaussian class lies properly inside Lin et al.'s underlying common-marginal conditional-optimal-transport information model; it is not asserted to lie inside their separate compact-support theorem class, so no Gaussian converse is transferred there without truncation or approximation. Sample-split Wald coverage on \(\Theta_+(\nu_*)\) and conservative projection coverage on all of \(\Theta\), including equality laws, are finite-dimensional inference specializations rather than novelty claims. No locally shortest equality-boundary interval is claimed.
body.interpretation: The exact frontier separates three regimes. With one selected covariate, every admissible positive-denominator ratio is a singleton ratio, so \(\rho_1(K,R)=1\). When \(R=1\), the residual floor and variance ceiling force all covariate-outcome scores to vanish, so the endpoint gain is identically zero and the ratio convention again gives one. For \(k\ge2\) and \(R>1\), \(\rho_k(K,R)=k/\{1+(k-1)KR\}\), which decreases to \(1/(KR)\) as the budget grows. The exact population greedy certificate is therefore \(1-\{1-\rho_k(K,R)/k\}^k\), while \(1-e^{-\rho_k(K,R)}\) is a simpler lower envelope. These are guarantees for tightening the observed-law endpoint \(B(S)\); they do not identify \(\tau_2\) beyond the maintained conditional-transport restrictions. Independent evaluation separates optimization from inference: ordinary Wald inference applies away from endpoint equality, and moment projection remains conservative on the whole compact parameter image.
